  • Métis↗Specific Métis government and community connection
    Connection & source
    Specific Métis government and community connection

    Métis Nation–Saskatchewan explicitly identifies itself as a government representing Métis citizens in Saskatchewan. The same page describes the Métis as a distinct Indigenous people. This supports a specific Saskatchewan route without making this government equivalent to all Métis communities. Inspection: Actual HTML body lines 9–17 and institutional address context, lines 23–26, inspected. Original metisnationsk.com/governance/ redirected to mns.ca. Limits: The institution’s membership definition and wider homeland account are not applied as universal eligibility rules. Métis identity is not used as a generic synonym for any person with mixed ancestry. No exclusive territorial boundary or claim to represent all Métis political perspectives is made.

    Current public institutional description inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Nêhiyaw↗Overlapping Cree/Plains Cree naming access point
    Connection & source
    Overlapping Cree/Plains Cree naming access point

    Neal McLeod's article identifies nêhiyawak as the Plains Cree self-name and explicitly places Cree communities across Saskatchewan. The Nêhiyaw directory route therefore connects to Saskatchewan as an overlapping Cree/Plains Cree naming access point, without creating an additional distinct-nation count. Inspection: Read the complete article; mapped evidence comes from the opening naming/geography paragraph and the following discussion of regional dialect differences. Limits: The article prints the plural nêhiyawak; this map record does not claim to be a singular-form dictionary analysis. Do not equate every regional Cree dialect, community, or government, or treat Plains Cree as the only Cree identity. No current population, migration-date, ceremony, or treaty-rights conclusion is taken from this article.

    Regional overview, undated; inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Plains Cree↗Specific language community connection
    Connection & source
    Specific language community connection

    Coauthor Dorothy Thunder is identified as a first-language Plains Cree speaker from Little Pine First Nation in Saskatchewan. This is one specific language-community connection within a wider Cree continuum; it does not define all Plains Cree geography or present fluency. Inspection: Actual author biography, line 59, with introductory naming/context section. The page warns that information dates from 2019; current career details and opinions are not generalized.

    Biographical account published August 5, 2019. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

    Connection & source

    Asikinack identifies Saulteaux as Plains Ojibway and explicitly lists associated communities in Saskatchewan. Only that broad geographic connection is adopted; the essay's treaty-cession characterization is not adopted.
